title: Begin the Beguine session and the Lincoln Hotel sensation
summary: The Spring 1938 sessions produce 'Begin the Beguine', 'Back Bay Shuffle' and 'Indian Love Call'; the hit saves the band, which reopens the Lincoln Hotel and films a short.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Name some of these great records you made with Artie Shaw. Some of them.
Well, I'm getting to that -- we're coming right in to it next.
What were some of these records, Cliff? 'Begin the Beguine,' did you say?
Yeah, 'Back Bay Shuffle,' 'Indian Love Call' -- all in the same day.
The same day, huh? What year was that?
1938, in the Spring.
Great.
And we left town, he was thinking of dissolving the band, but he had a commitment in a hotel in St. Louis and he couldn't take Billie Holiday down there,

so he hired a new singer called Helen Forrest. And we went to St. Louis, and in the middle of the engagement, after a week or two in St. Louis, he got a call one day from RCA Victor -- this is only two months later -- from RCA Victor, from Leonard Joy who was a big man there, saying to come back. He was already gonna dissolve the band, now. But Begin the Beguine and the record date is a sensation, it is sweeping the nation.
Well, as a bunch of kids, you don't know how thrilled we were. So we booked one date, we had a battle of music with some band, the house band, at the Savoy in Chicago.
The Savoy in Chicago -- do you remember, was it Erskine Tate?
One night on the way back -- I can't recall.
Okay.
And then, they had us booked in to the Lincoln Hotel, because they reopened. We reopened the Lincoln Hotel.
When was this?
Oh, it must have been May or June.
But what town? Lincoln Hotel where?
New York City.
Okay.

And we were a sensation. That's when they came in with all the contracts and so forth. During that time, we made the one movie I made, which was a short subject at their studios, and for the jazz archives -- we did 'Begin the Beguine' in a Warner Brothers short subject.
